title: Remediation is detecting problems but failing to fix them

maxFailPct.text: Share of detected issues left unfixed before the remediation is ineffective

report.title: {Items.Count} {Plural(Items.Count, 'remediation is', 'remediations are')} failing to fix what they find

messages.businessImpact: The problem is known, reported and untreated, which is worse than not looking, because the report suggests something is being done.
remediation: Check the run-as context and whether the fix needs rights the script does not have.
messages.cannotSee: What is counted as unfixed is worked out from what Intune says it fixed, rather than from the counts Graph keeps of remediations that errored or changed nothing: the fixed figure is the one the console shows an administrator, so this agrees with the screen they are looking at. The consequence is that a device between running the repair and reporting the result is counted as unfixed until it reports, so a remediation assigned this morning can appear here and be gone by tomorrow. The detected count divides every device by what detection found, and a device Intune has since fixed is still counted there, which is why the share is worked out against the devices the repair was actually run on. A device the repair was never run on, which is what an assignment set to detect only produces, is taken out of both. Why a repair failed is not read, and whether detection was right about there being a problem is not visible: a detection script that is too eager makes work for a repair script that cannot succeed.
